content:
# Disagreement Log — 2 Maccabees Chapter 8

**Date:** 2026-03-17
**Agents:** EMET, LOGOS, PNEUMA
**Total Disagreements:** 22

---

## Disagreement 001 — v. 1: Recruitment method

- **EMET:** "secretly entered the villages and summoned their kinsmen"
- **LOGOS:** "went about secretly into the villages, summoning their kinsfolk"
- **PNEUMA:** "began moving through the villages secretly, rallying family members"
- **Note:** "Summoning" (EMET/LOGOS) vs. "rallying" (PNEUMA). Greek *proskaleitai*. LOGOS is most accurate. SOPHIA follows LOGOS.

## Disagreement 002 — v. 2: Prayer framing

- **EMET:** "they entreated the LORD to look upon the people who were oppressed by all"
- **LOGOS:** "they called upon the LORD to look upon the people who were being oppressed on every side"
- **PNEUMA:** "They prayed to the LORD: look at your people, crushed on every side"
- **Note:** PNEUMA converts to direct address in the prayer. LOGOS's "on every side" for Greek *pantothen* is accurate. SOPHIA uses LOGOS.

## Disagreement 003 — v. 4: "lawless destruction"

- **EMET:** "the lawless destruction of the innocent babies"
- **LOGOS:** "the lawless destruction of the innocent children"
- **PNEUMA:** "the massacre of innocent children"
- **Note:** "Babies" (EMET) for Greek *nēpiōn* — infants/babies. LOGOS uses "children" more broadly. EMET is more precise. SOPHIA uses "innocent children" per LOGOS for the broader context.

## Disagreement 004 — v. 5: Gentiles' inability to stop Judas

- **EMET:** "the Gentiles could not withstand him"
- **LOGOS:** "the Gentiles found him irresistible"
- **PNEUMA:** "the Gentiles found him impossible to stop"
- **Note:** LOGOS and PNEUMA are functionally equivalent. EMET is simpler. SOPHIA uses "irresistible" per LOGOS.

## Disagreement 005 — v. 6: "won back" vs. "retook"

- **EMET:** "He won back the most advantageous positions"
- **LOGOS:** "retook the most favorable positions"
- **PNEUMA:** "retaking key positions"
- **Note:** LOGOS and PNEUMA agree on "retook/retaking." EMET's "won back" is acceptable. SOPHIA follows LOGOS.

## Disagreement 006 — v. 7: Night attacks

- **EMET:** "His valor was talked about everywhere"
- **LOGOS:** "His bravery was talked about everywhere"
- **PNEUMA:** "His courage became the talk of the region"
- **Note:** "Valor" (EMET) vs. "bravery" (LOGOS) vs. "courage" (PNEUMA) for Greek *andreia*. "Valor" is more formal. SOPHIA uses "valor" as it fits the military register.

## Disagreement 007 — v. 8: Philip's observation

- **EMET:** "the man was gaining ground little by little and that he was pushing ahead with greater and greater frequency and success"
- **LOGOS:** "the man was gaining ground gradually, and that his advances in frequency and success were becoming more and more pronounced"
- **PNEUMA:** "this man was growing stronger with each passing week. The attacks were becoming more frequent, the victories more decisive"
- **Note:** PNEUMA paraphrases freely. EMET and LOGOS are closer. SOPHIA follows LOGOS's formulation.

## Disagreement 008 — v. 9: Nicanor's title

- **EMET:** "one of the king's First Friends"
- **LOGOS:** "one of the king's First Friends"
- **PNEUMA:** "one of the king's top officials"
- **Note:** EMET and LOGOS preserve the technical Seleucid court title "First Friends" (*protōn philōn*). PNEUMA uses a generic translation. SOPHIA follows EMET/LOGOS.

## Disagreement 009 — v. 10: Method of tribute

- **EMET:** "determined to make up for the king the tribute due to the Romans"
- **LOGOS:** "resolved to raise for the king the tribute owed to the Romans"
- **PNEUMA:** "he would cover the two-thousand-talent tribute owed to Rome by selling the Jews"
- **Note:** PNEUMA integrates the amount into this verse. EMET/LOGOS defer the amount to v. 10 as in the Greek. SOPHIA follows LOGOS.

## Disagreement 010 — v. 11: "not anticipating"

- **EMET:** "not anticipating the judgment that was about to overtake him"
- **LOGOS:** "little anticipating the judgment that was about to overtake him"
- **PNEUMA:** "He had no idea what was about to fall on him"
- **Note:** LOGOS's "little anticipating" adds ironic emphasis. PNEUMA's paraphrase loses the formal irony. SOPHIA uses "little anticipating."

## Disagreement 011 — v. 13: Deserters

- **EMET:** "those who were cowardly and distrustful of God's justice ran off and got out of the way"
- **LOGOS:** "those who were cowardly and had lost faith in God's justice deserted and made off"
- **PNEUMA:** "The ones who panicked — those whose faith in God's justice had crumbled — slipped away and disappeared"
- **Note:** LOGOS's "deserted" is the most precise military term. PNEUMA's "slipped away and disappeared" is too mild for desertion in context. SOPHIA follows LOGOS.

## Disagreement 012 — v. 16: Judas's exhortation

- **EMET:** "exhorted them not to be frightened by the enemy and not to fear the great multitude of Gentiles"
- **LOGOS:** "exhorted them not to be panic-stricken at the enemy or to be frightened by the great multitude"
- **PNEUMA:** "don't let the enemy intimidate you. Don't let the numbers frighten you"
- **Note:** PNEUMA converts to direct address throughout the speech. LOGOS distinguishes panic (*ekplessō*) from fright (*kataplēssō*). SOPHIA follows LOGOS.

## Disagreement 013 — v. 17: "cruel mockery"

- **EMET:** "the torture of the derided city"
- **LOGOS:** "the cruel mockery done to the city"
- **PNEUMA:** "the humiliation of the city"
- **Note:** Greek *empaigmon* — mockery/ridicule. LOGOS's "cruel mockery" captures both the violence and the contempt. EMET's "torture of the derided city" is awkward. SOPHIA uses "cruel mockery."

## Disagreement 014 — v. 18: "single nod"

- **EMET:** "who is able with a single nod to strike down those who are coming against us and even the whole world"
- **LOGOS:** "who with a single nod is able to strike down not only those advancing against us but even the whole world"
- **PNEUMA:** "who with a single nod can bring down every one of those men advancing on us — and the whole world besides"
- **Note:** All three capture the "single nod" image well. LOGOS adds "not only... but even" which is more precise to the Greek. SOPHIA follows LOGOS.

## Disagreement 015 — v. 19: Sennacherib reference

- **EMET:** "how in the time of Sennacherib a hundred and eighty-five thousand had perished"
- **LOGOS:** "how in the days of Sennacherib, a hundred and eighty-five thousand had been destroyed"
- **PNEUMA:** "In the days of Sennacherib, one hundred and eighty-five thousand men had been destroyed overnight"
- **Note:** PNEUMA adds "overnight" for dramatic color. The Greek does not specify this (though it is consistent with 2 Kings 19:35). SOPHIA follows LOGOS.

## Disagreement 016 — v. 21: Preparation for battle

- **EMET:** "made them ready to die for their laws and their country"
- **LOGOS:** "made them ready to die for their laws and their fatherland"
- **PNEUMA:** "They were ready to die for the law and for their country"
- **Note:** "Fatherland" (LOGOS) vs. "country" (EMET/PNEUMA) for Greek *patris*. "Fatherland" is a more literal and formal translation. SOPHIA uses "fatherland."

## Disagreement 017 — v. 23: Scripture reading

- **EMET:** "appointed Eleazar to read aloud from the holy book"
- **LOGOS:** "appointed Eleazar to read aloud from the holy scriptures"
- **PNEUMA:** "He appointed Eleazar to read publicly from the holy scriptures"
- **Note:** "Holy book" (EMET) vs. "holy scriptures" (LOGOS/PNEUMA). Greek *tēn hieran biblon*. "Holy scriptures" better represents the canonical sense. SOPHIA follows LOGOS.

## Disagreement 018 — v. 25: Pursuit broken off

- **EMET:** "they were obliged to return because the hour was late"
- **LOGOS:** "they had to break off because the hour was late"
- **PNEUMA:** "They chased the fleeing enemy until they had to stop — the hour was too late to continue"
- **Note:** PNEUMA adds detail ("fleeing enemy"). LOGOS is clean. SOPHIA follows LOGOS.

## Disagreement 019 — v. 27: Sabbath observance after battle

- **EMET:** "they kept the sabbath, giving abundant praise and thanks to the LORD"
- **LOGOS:** "they kept the sabbath, offering abundant praise and thanks to the LORD"
- **PNEUMA:** "They kept the sabbath — with abundant praise and thanks to the LORD"
- **Note:** "Giving" (EMET) vs. "offering" (LOGOS) vs. no difference in substance. SOPHIA uses "offering."

## Disagreement 020 — v. 30: Distribution of spoils — recipients

- **EMET:** "giving shares equal to their own to those who had been tortured and to the orphans and widows and also to the elderly"
- **LOGOS:** "giving equal shares to those who had been tortured, to the orphans, the widows, and the elderly"
- **PNEUMA:** "equal shares for those who had suffered torture, for the orphans, for the widows, for the elderly"
- **Note:** All three agree on the recipients. EMET adds "equal to their own" — Greek *isa merē* — equal shares. SOPHIA retains this detail: "equal shares."

## Disagreement 021 — v. 34: Nicanor's characterization

- **EMET:** "The thrice-accursed Nicanor"
- **LOGOS:** "The three-times-accursed Nicanor"
- **PNEUMA:** "Nicanor — the wretch three times cursed"
- **Note:** Greek *triskataratos* — thrice-accursed. EMET's "thrice-accursed" is a traditional rendering; LOGOS's "three-times-accursed" is more transparent; PNEUMA's "wretch three times cursed" adds "wretch." SOPHIA uses "three-times-accursed."

## Disagreement 022 — v. 36: Nicanor's testimony

- **EMET:** "proclaimed that the Jews had a champion and that the Jews were invulnerable because they followed the laws ordained by him"
- **LOGOS:** "declared publicly that the Jews had a defender, and that they were invulnerable because they followed the laws he had ordained"
- **PNEUMA:** "ended up telling everyone the opposite story: the Jews have a protector. Following God's laws makes them untouchable"
- **Note:** "Champion" (EMET) vs. "defender" (LOGOS) vs. "protector" (PNEUMA) for Greek *prostaten*. LOGOS's "defender" is precise. PNEUMA's "untouchable" loses the specific meaning of *anepicheirētos* — not to be attacked/unapproachable in battle. SOPHIA uses "invulnerable" per EMET/LOGOS.
